text:
alex: Ran an nsys capture against the v2 serving job (8x A10) — timeline looks off. kernels are high-util but there's lots of white space between H2D memcpy and kernels, and the host shows long API blocks. wondering if this is stream-syncing or CPU preemption. :thinking:
sophia: can you paste the nsys command and a timeline snippet? also attach the .qdrep if you pushed it to s3. :eyes:
alex: command I used:```nsys profile --output out --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sample=none --force-overwrite --quiet -- ./run_inference.sh --workers=32```Uploaded qdrep to s3://redwood-perf/1769205801.qdrep. Timeline: at ~00:00:12 there are repeated small host->device memcpy bursts (~100-200us) on the default stream immediately followed by kernels that start 1-2ms later. Kernels are single-stream, high SM utilization, but they never overlap with the memcpy bursts. Host thread shows many `sched_yield` / `futex_wait` entries around the same time.
raj: default stream memcpy can serialize with kernels depending on stream usage — if memcpys are sync (cudaMemcpy) or using default stream they can cause implicit synchronization. Try switching to cudaMemcpyAsync into a non-default stream or use pinned host memory so async actually avoids blocking. Also check that you're not mixing stream priorities.
matt: the `sched_yield` spikes smell like the Python thread pool getting preempted. If the CPU handling enqueues/copies is starved the GPU will be idle waiting on memcpy. What's the CPU runqueue during the capture? Did nsys show long CPU 'API' blocks (the orange CPU lane) or short bursts?
alex: nsys shows long API blocks on the main worker thread (~5-20ms) which then call into `cuMemcpy`/`cuLaunchKernel`. The odd part is the memcpy appears as blocking memcpy (not async) in the timeline — even though code uses `torch.Tensor.pin_memory()` and `stream.synchronize()` only occasionally. Maybe our batching logic is falling back to sync memcpy for small tensors.
sophia: two quick tests: 1) force use of `cudaMemcpyAsync` + explicit stream and capture again; 2) allocate host buffers with `posix_memalign`/pinned and measure memcpy latency. Also try `NSYS_NVTX_FORCE=1` to get clearer NVTX markers.
raj: another angle: small H2D copies (lots of tiny transfers) cause PCIe overheads and kernel queue gaps. Consider coalescing copies (aggregate tensors into a staging buffer) or increase your batcher window to combine requests into larger contiguous transfers. Batching heuristic: if seq_len < 64, accumulate up to N requests or until T ms. Tunable.
matt: CPU scheduling gap fix: bump process niceness / use thread affinity so copy thread stays on a core. On Linux we've seen better tail latency when copy threads are pinned and using SCHED_BATCH/SCHED_FIFO (test carefully). Also check if the machine has irqbalance picking cores for PCIe interrupts — can move interrupts to same NUMA node as GPU.
alex: KV cache detail — when warmup happens we do big device uploads to populate KV. In some traces the initial KV memcpy is huge and blocks everything for ~30ms. Can we incrementalize KV uploads and keep a device-resident pool so later requests avoid that hit?
sophia: yes, incremental KV prefetch is low-risk. Also set a device cache reservation per model instance to avoid repeated allocations/copies. That plus pinned staging buffers should reduce the H2D stall.
ci-bot: perf note recorded: ticket PERF-5234 created with trace s3://redwood-perf/1769205801.qdrep — assigned to @raj and @matt.
raj: one more profiler tip: re-run with `nsys profile --sample=none --trace=cuda,osrt,nvtx --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --capture-start-stop` and place NVTX start/stop around the request pipeline. This gives precise per-request windows and avoids noise from background housekeeping. Also capture `--export=timeline.json` for perfetto if you want flamegraph zooming.
alex: will run the async/pinned/coalesce experiments today and upload new traces. Action items: (1) try cudaMemcpyAsync + non-default streams + pinned host memory, (2) implement staging buffer to coalesce small H2D copies, (3) reserve device KV memory and incremental uploads, (4) pin copy threads / test affinity. I'll post updated qdrep. Thanks all :thumbsup:
